publication.title: IDF destroys Hezbollah's underground command complex beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge, then withdraws
publication.summary: After a months-long operation the IDF's 36th Division demolished a Hezbollah tunnel network beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon and withdrew, in what open-source defense analysts describe as a step toward consolidating the ceasefire.
publication.body:
The Israel Defense Forces has completed an operation, reported under the codename "Chisel of Flames," to dismantle a Hezbollah underground complex beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, according to the IDF and multiple outlets covering the campaign, including the Jerusalem Post, The Times of Israel and the open-source defense outlet FDD's Long War Journal.

According to these reports, the IDF's 36th Division identified the site as a central command complex and "nerve center" for Hezbollah's Badr Unit, describing it as the last and most significant line of Hezbollah defense in southern Lebanon after roughly two decades of Iranian-backed construction. The IDF says the underground network ran across some 14 tunnel routes totaling about 5.4 kilometers, and that its forces used roughly 1,100 tons of explosives to destroy more than two kilometers of the infrastructure. Israeli forces reported finding command rooms, weapons storage rooms, generators, living quarters and a kitchen inside the complex, and described dozens of entrenched fighters, estimated at around 50, having occupied it during the operation.

The IDF released footage of the site's destruction and described what remains of the ridge as "nothing more than a sandbox." Israeli forces have since withdrawn from the ridge. The Meir Amit Intelligence and Terrorism Information Center's analysis frames the operation as intended to advance the ceasefire arrangement between Israel and Lebanon by removing a Hezbollah strongpoint near the border rather than as the opening of a new front.

The operation followed weeks of contested efforts over the ridge, including Hezbollah attacks and stalled handover arrangements, according to Long War Journal's reporting. Hezbollah has continued limited attacks elsewhere along the border since the ridge operation concluded, including drone launches toward IDF positions that Israeli forces say they intercepted.

This account is drawn from IDF statements as relayed by the cited outlets and from open-source defense analysis; Lions of Zion has not independently verified troop numbers or explosive tonnages beyond what these sources report.

publication.title: Documentary alleges IDF used AI to kill Gaza civilians; IDF says strike decisions were made only by people
publication.summary: A documentary by Israeli filmmakers, NAZA, alleges the IDF's targeting process amounted to AI-driven mass-casualty strikes on Gaza civilians. The IDF categorically rejects the allegation and says the anonymous testimonies it relies on cannot be verified.
publication.body:
A documentary made by Israeli filmmakers, titled "NAZA," premiered at the Venice International Film Festival and, according to The Jerusalem Post and The Times of Israel, received a lengthy standing ovation. The film is reported to allege, based on anonymous testimony from individuals described as having worked within IDF systems, that the military's use of AI-assisted tools in Gaza amounted to indiscriminate or mass-casualty targeting of civilians.

The IDF Spokesperson's Unit issued a categorical rejection of the film's central claims. According to The Times of Israel, the military said that decisions on selecting and approving strikes were made "by human personnel only... and not by artificial intelligence," and that the documentary relied on anonymous testimonies whose speakers' identities and military roles could not be independently verified.

Lions of Zion has not viewed the film or the underlying testimonies and cannot independently confirm either the specific claims made in the documentary or the IDF's characterization of them. Both the film's premiere and the IDF's public rebuttal are independently reported by multiple outlets, but the substantive question — what role, if any, AI-assisted systems played in specific strike decisions — remains contested between the filmmakers and the military and is not resolved by either side's public statements alone.

publication.title: Technion researchers unveil drug-free nanoparticles that halt aggressive breast cancer tumors
publication.summary: Technion bioengineers built biomimetic nanoparticles, called MPsomes, that block tumor-supporting immune cells without delivering any drug, and slowed triple-negative breast cancer growth in mouse models as effectively as existing treatments.
publication.body:
Researchers at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology have developed a nanomedicine approach that inhibits aggressive triple-negative breast cancer without delivering any drug, antibody or chemotherapy agent, according to the Technion's own announcement and a peer-reviewed paper in ACS Nano, corroborated by independent coverage from The Times of Israel and EurekAlert.

Rather than attacking cancer cells directly, the approach targets the tumor's surrounding environment. Macrophages, white blood cells whose normal role is to protect the body, are often "hijacked" by tumors, which use them to support their own growth and blunt the immune system's response. The Technion team's nanoparticles, called MPsomes, act as a biological decoy: they compete with immune cells for binding sites in the tumor microenvironment and block harmful cells' access to the tumor.

In cell cultures and in preclinical mouse models of triple-negative breast cancer — a form of the disease with limited treatment options — the particles accumulated in high concentrations around tumors and inhibited their growth with effectiveness the researchers describe as comparable to existing treatments. The Technion also reports a manufacturing process capable of producing about 20 milliliters of the nanoparticles per minute, roughly 1.2 liters per hour, a scale the university says supports further development toward clinical use.

The work has so far been demonstrated in cell cultures and animal models; it has not yet been tested in human clinical trials, and Lions of Zion is not aware of a published timeline for human studies.
